nodes.description: Disruption of the endothelial barrier raises vascular permeability and supports the leak/bleeding arm of OHF, connecting the NS1 endothelial effect to petechial and more severe hemorrhagic manifestations.

evidence.reference_title: Orthoflavivirus omskense NS1 Protein Induces Microvascular Endothelial Permeability In Vitro.
evidence.snippet: RNAseq of endothelial cells treated with OHFV NS1 indicated that OHFV NS1 enhances the expression of genes associated with cellular stress responses, vascular signaling, and cell-cell junction regulation, resulting in a nonspecific increase in the endothelial permeability of various vessels.

nodes.description: The secreted OHFV NS1 protein acts directly on human lung microvascular and umbilical-vein endothelial cells in vitro, increasing expression programs associated with stress, vascular signaling and junction regulation. This disrupts endothelial barrier function and is the best-supported Omsk-specific bridge from viral replication into the vascular injury shared by hemorrhagic fevers.

evidence.reference_title: Orthoflavivirus omskense NS1 Protein Induces Microvascular Endothelial Permeability In Vitro.
evidence.snippet: It was shown that recombinant OHFV NS1 produced in eucaryotic cells directly affects both human lung microvascular endothelial cells (HLMVEC) and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) in vitro.

nodes.description: After inoculation from a tick bite or contaminated muskrat exposure, OHFV enters susceptible mammalian cells and replicates as a flaviviral RNA genome. The available Omsk-specific replicon/VLP system demonstrates that OHFV replicon RNA can express reporter genes in mammalian cells harboring replicating viral RNA.

evidence.reference_title: Sub-genomic replicon and virus-like particles of Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus.
evidence.snippet: GFP and luciferase genes were inserted into the OHFV replicon, and these reporter genes were expressed in cells harboring replicating replicon RNA.
